Alerts proposed: Place the order

Each is its own alert. When one fires, follow its own entry in the runbook. Thresholds, windows and whether an alert pages a person are the operators’ values, not set here.

Checkouts that ended with no order

Its entry in the runbook ›

The question it answersHow many checkouts reaching Ordering API ended without their order being written?
What it counts

Ordering-api log over the window, by request id: those with a 'Sending command:' line for the create command and no 'CreateOrderCommand succeeded - RequestId:' line, that is the 'CreateOrderCommand failed - RequestId:' lines and the requests that threw before answering; against all such request ids. A retried call carries the same request id and counts once

Counted on cases.

Why it is proposed

a checkout that reaches Ordering API and writes no order leaves the customer with no order and, on the web front end, an emptied basket and the orders page, so the customer is not told.

  • A checkout that never reaches Ordering API fails in front of the customer and is not counted here.
  • Nor is an order call refused at authentication, which writes no command line (Ordering API's answers by status show it).
Which cases its entry works

By the move the case left by: “The order is placed” from the case is created.

Its runbook entry works that state's tests.

ThresholdOperator value, not set here. For each measure, the value at which the alert fires. Whether it pages a person, opens a ticket or shows on a dashboard is the operators' decision.
WindowOperator value, not set here. How long the condition must hold before it fires. What the design assumes about time: Expected outcome: The order is placed — WebApp's HTTP clients carry the standard resilience handler; a repeated POST with the same x-requestid is answered without a second order; Process step 1.1: The customer's basket is emptied — No timeout of its own. The WebApp's basket delete is a gRPC call whose client is made by the HTTP client factory, so it carries the standard resilience handler: each attempt 10 seconds, up to 3 retries, 30 seconds in all. Basket API's delete on OrderStartedIntegrationEvent has no clock: the message waits in queue Basket until it is consumed, and the queue sets no expiry.
No dataIt also fires when its measure cannot be counted for longer than the window. A count that finds no events in a window is zero, not missing data. A count fails when what it is read from is down; What it counts says where that is.
Symptom, not causeIt fires on what happens to cases, not on any component’s errors. Telling causes apart is the runbook’s job.
Exists todayyes

Companion measures

Read by the runbook’s checks, not proposed for alerting:

  • Order requests answered OK with no order created
  • Ordering API requests by route and status, and their duration
  • Ordering database accepting connections
  • Long-running statements on orderingdb
  • Connections to the postgres server against max_connections
